title: SatSure Raises 600 Million Rupees From Government-Backed Space Fund at 8.7 Billion Valuation
excerpt: The Bengaluru satellite-data startup's ongoing 2 billion rupee Series B values it at 8.7 billion rupees post-money, as the IN-SPACe-anchored Antariksh Venture Capital Fund backs India's private space push.
body:
• Bengaluru-based SatSure has raised 600 million rupees ($7 million) from the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund as part of an ongoing 2 billion rupee Series B round, the company said on Friday.
  • The investment values SatSure at 8.7 billion rupees ($93 million) post-money. The 16 billion rupee Antariksh fund is anchored by IN-SPACe, India's private space sector regulator, and managed by SIDBI Venture Capital.
  • The round comprises 1.65 billion rupees in fresh equity, 250 million rupees in venture debt and 100 million rupees in secondary transactions, and the company expects to close it by December 2026.
  • The proceeds will help prepare SatSure's satellite imaging payloads for launch in 2027, support its participation in India's planned Earth-observation satellite network, and expand its data analysis capabilities and international operations.

SatSure, a Bengaluru startup that turns satellite imagery into decisions for banks, insurers and governments, has raised 600 million rupees ($7 million) from a government-backed space technology fund, the company said on Friday. The investment from the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund is part of an ongoing Series B round of 2 billion rupees and values SatSure at 8.7 billion rupees ($93 million) post-money, according to Reuters.

What SatSure does

"The fundraise takes the total SatSure has raised from institutional investors to 4.27 billion rupees, excluding grants."

SatSure uses satellite imagery and artificial intelligence to help banks, insurers, infrastructure firms and government agencies make decisions — monitoring crops, infrastructure and climate risks from orbit, as Finimize summarised the business. Its named customers include HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, ITC, Bayer and the Airports Authority of India. Its subsidiary KaleidEO develops satellite imaging systems for Earth observation — the hardware side of a business that has mostly sold analysis of other people's satellite data.

The round and the fund behind it

The Series B is structured as 1.65 billion rupees in fresh equity, 250 million rupees in venture debt and 100 million rupees in secondary transactions, in which existing shareholders sell shares rather than the company issuing new ones. The company expects to close the round by December 2026. The cheque announced on Friday comes from the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund, a 16 billion rupee fund anchored by IN-SPACe — the regulator for India's private space sector — and managed by SIDBI Venture Capital, an arm of the state-owned small-business lender SIDBI.

The investment lands in the middle of a deliberate policy push. India has been expanding its commercial space industry through reforms that opened a traditionally state-dominated sector to private companies and investors, and a sovereign fund anchored by the sector's own regulator is one of the instruments of that push: public money taking equity positions in the private companies the reforms are meant to create.

What the money is for

SatSure said the proceeds will help prepare its satellite imaging payloads for launch in 2027, support its participation in India's planned Earth-observation satellite network, and expand its data analysis capabilities and international operations. The fundraise takes the total SatSure has raised from institutional investors to 4.27 billion rupees, excluding grants. Its previous backers include Baring Private Equity Partners India, Promus Ventures and Asian Development Bank Ventures.

What to watch next is execution against two dated commitments: the Series B is expected to close by December 2026, and the payloads the money is preparing are slated for launch in 2027. Both are company statements of intent, not completed milestones — the round is ongoing, and Friday's announcement covers 600 million rupees of the 2 billion rupee total.
